sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports animation and icon tools
sections.what: Brings in the animation library and the lightning icon.
sections.why: Likely reason: the splash uses motion and a logo icon. Reason not stated.

sections.name: AuthViewLoading (part 1)
sections.title: Logo and startup title
sections.what: Draws the dark background, soft glows, a spinning and pulsing logo tile, the MOMENTUM OS title and the startup line.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a branded first impression while the workspace loads.
sections.watch_out: The title says MOMENTUM OS while the login screen says MOMENTUM PRO, so the brand name is inconsistent.

sections.name: AuthViewLoading (part 2)
sections.title: Sliding loading bar
sections.what: Draws a thin bar that slides across endlessly beneath the text to show that work is happening.
sections.why: Likely reason: a common sign that something is still running. It does not measure real progress.
sections.watch_out: The bar does not reflect real progress, so it keeps moving even if the app is stuck.

summary: A full-screen loading splash shown while the workspace is being prepared.
purpose: Shows the user that the app is working, so the screen is not blank.
why: Likely reason: avoids a blank screen during startup. The code does not say when it appears.
how: Shows a dark full screen with two soft glows, a rotating and pulsing logo, the title MOMENTUM OS and a line saying the workspace is initializing. A bar slides back and forth underneath. All of it animates continuously and takes no input.
inputs: None. It takes no props or data.
outputs: An animated screen only. Nothing is saved.
risks: The animation runs until the screen is replaced, which is normal for a loader. Its title says MOMENTUM OS while the login screen says MOMENTUM PRO, which is inconsistent. It is a default export, unlike most files here, so the import style must match.
debug: If the splash stays on screen, the problem is probably in the startup logic that decides when to show it, not in this file. If it looks different from the login screen, compare the title text with AuthView.
